stemMd: At which event in normal meiosis does reduction from two homologous chromosome sets to one set per daughter nucleus occur?

options.label: D
options.textMd: Separation of homologous chromosomes in the first meiotic division

options.label: E
options.textMd: Separation of sister chromatids in mitosis

explanationMd: During meiosis I, homologous chromosomes separate while sister chromatids remain together. Each daughter nucleus receives one chromosome of each homologous pair, reducing ploidy. Meiosis II then separates sister chromatids without a second reduction in the number of homologous sets.

distractorRationale.c: Replication doubles DNA content rather than reducing homologous sets.
distractorRationale.a: Fertilization restores two sets rather than reducing them.
distractorRationale.b: Translation does not partition chromosome sets.
